# @yogeshhrathod/qivi

> Provider-independent React 19 particle avatar library. Requires react-dom 19 and three ^0.180.0. No speech-provider SDK, API key, network request, or language model is included.

- [Integration and customization guide](docs/performance.md): public API, character profiles, visual presentation, expression extensions, shapes, audio synchronization, cancellation, and call-only integration.
- [README](README.md): installation, package builds, baseline components and voice sources.
- [Avatar props and imperative handle](dist/QiviAvatar.d.ts): authoritative TypeScript interfaces.
- [Performance timeline](dist/performance.d.ts): cues and clock/media controller.
- [Presets and parameter definitions](dist/presets.d.ts): BASE, Params, expression and personality definitions.

## Rules for integrating agents

1. Render QiviAvatar in a client component and import @yogeshhrathod/qivi/styles.css once.
2. Activity and emotion are independent: state="talking", expression="concern" is supported.
3. Use QiviVoice.fromMediaElement(audio) for waveform-driven speech animation. Use QiviPerformance for semantic expression/shape/character cues. Waveforms alone do not infer emotion or phoneme visemes.
4. Cue at/duration and update()/play() clocks use SECONDS relative to the audio. Convert provider millisecond timestamps before passing them.
5. QiviPerformance follows the actual playback clock, not text length or network arrival times. Use followMedia(audio), or play(() => yourClockInSeconds).
6. Pass the mounted QiviAvatarHandle to new QiviPerformance(handle, cues). Dispose the controller on interruption/unmount. It restores current component props and cancels queued reactions. Audio and QiviVoice must be stopped/disposed separately by the host.
7. Set autoEmote=false when authoring explicit impulses to avoid duplicate automatic gestures. Use reducedMotion="auto" by default.
8. For expressive calls use expressionStrength around 1.3–1.7. Range is 0–2. This differs from intensity (0–1 body deformation). Avoid extrapolating parameter values blindly.
9. QiviCharacter supports name, personality, theme, shape, presentation, params, and behavior. Explicit personality/shape props override profile defaults; theme="auto" uses the profile palette. A performance frame replaces the prior overlay; it is not a persistent patch.
10. masculine/feminine/neutral presentation changes particle proportions and eyes only. Voice and behavioral personality are independent. No human model, hair, clothing, or gendered behavior is implied.
11. customShape is a positive radial silhouette. Prefer createRadialShape(angle => radius); it validates radius 0.1–2. Holes and arbitrary meshes are unsupported.
12. Static fallback preserves palette and supported face customization but does not animate or render morph silhouettes. Do not promise morphing under quality="static", under 48px, or without WebGL.
13. Provider credentials belong in the host server. Convert provider timing and semantic intent into plain QiviPerformanceCue objects. Do not couple this library to ElevenLabs.

## Character versions

CHARACTERS.qivi is neutral; CHARACTERS.female is Nova; CHARACTERS.male is Sol; CHARACTERS.ember is a playful amber star; CHARACTERS.sage is a calm mint companion; CHARACTERS.atlas is a protective midnight shield. Each is an editable QiviCharacter profile. New QiviPersonality bases spark and diplomat can be paired with any presentation or voice. Read docs/performance.md for examples.
